alerts.name: OutboxLagHigh
alerts.description: The oldest still-due outbox row has been waiting longer than this system's own maximum legitimate cumulative retry-schedule age — delivery is genuinely stuck, not merely cooling down through an ordinary backoff cycle.
alerts.thresholdDerivation: outbox_lag_seconds measures a row's CUMULATIVE age since creation (PumpOnce's own time.Since(oldestCreatedAt), internal/app/outboxworker/builder.go), not the delay of any single retry — so platform.Timeouts.OutboxBackoffMax (300s), which bounds only ONE retry interval, is the wrong quantity to compare it against: a row that has legitimately retried several times accumulates far more than 300s of age with nothing wrong. The correct ceiling is the cumulative age a row reaches after exhausting domain/outbox.MaxAttempts (10, internal/domain/outbox/backoff.go) attempts. EvaluateBackoff's schedule with the shipped defaults (OutboxBackoffBase 30s, OutboxBackoffMax 300s) produces retry delays, per attempt 1 through 9 (attempt 10 is the dead-lettering attempt — no further delay is ever scheduled after it): 30s, 60s, 120s, 240s, 300s, 300s, 300s, 300s, 300s. Sum = 30+60+120+240+(300*5) = 1950s — the age at which a row's own FINAL legitimate attempt becomes due, the ceiling of 'still legitimately retrying, never yet given up.' Add worst-case real-world overhead per retry cycle — up to OutboxPumpInterval (5s, waiting for a tick to claim a just-due row) plus OutboxDeliveryTimeout (15s, the bounded worst case for the failing Deliver call itself, which elapses BEFORE recordFailure stamps the next backoff window) — across the 9 cycles between attempts 1-10: 9 * (5s+15s) = 180s. Worst-case legitimate age: 1950s + 180s = 2130s (35.5min). 2400s (40min) sits comfortably above that with headroom, so this alert now fires only once a row has plausibly exhausted its ENTIRE legitimate retry budget without yet being dead-lettered — a real stuck condition (e.g. the outbox worker loop itself wedged, or a DB issue silently blocking claims), never ordinary backoff.

alerts.name: OutboxDeadLetterAny
alerts.description: At least one outbox entry exhausted its full retry budget and was dead-lettered — a notification a user never received.
alerts.thresholdDerivation: Presence, not a rate: dead-lettering only happens after domain/outbox.MaxAttempts delivery attempts are exhausted (internal/app/outboxworker/builder.go) — there is no 'normal' rate of exhausting a full retry budget, so any occurrence at all is worth a look.

alerts.name: OrphanReapRateHigh
alerts.description: The reconciler is reaping orphaned provider-side sandboxes at a rate well above the single-race noise this mechanism is known to produce occasionally on its own.
alerts.thresholdDerivation: internal/app/reconciler/reconciler.go's own doc comment names an inherent, benign single-orphan case: a reconcile tick landing in the narrow window between a real CreateSandbox success and its provider_id actually committing looks, for exactly one tick, identical to a genuine orphan — an occasional single reap is expected, not a bug. 5 in one 10-minute window (10x platform.Timeouts.ReconcilerInterval, internal/platform/timeouts.go) is well above that noise floor and reads as a sustained pattern.

alerts.name: BootDurationP95High
alerts.description: In-sandbox boot-to-ready duration (post-connect: repo clone/sync through hook/service startup) has reached this system's own chosen anchor for how long boot as a whole is expected to comfortably take.
alerts.thresholdDerivation: Corrected (Phase 6 audit fix, Finding 1): an earlier version of this field claimed 240s (platform.Timeouts.FirstConnectBudget) was the literal ceiling EvaluateConnectingTimeout (internal/domain/sandbox/liveness.go) applies to a booting sandbox's TOTAL elapsed time — false. EvaluateConnectingTimeout measures elapsed time since the LAST liveness signal, using FirstConnectBudget (240s) only before the first signal ever arrives and the shorter SteadyHeartbeatBudget (90s) for every gap after that (§3.2: 'Boot-progress reports during long boots re-arm the connecting deadline'). Boot-progress reports fire throughout the docker/services phases and git_sync events fire throughout the gitclone phase -- both are recognized liveness signals, together spanning nearly the exact span this metric measures -- so the watchdog ceiling governing nearly all of it is 90s per gap, not 240s — and even that bounds only inter-signal gaps, never this metric's own cumulative total. TestResilienceScenario3_SlowBoot_SurvivesRepeatedBootProgressPings_NeverFalselyKilled (test/resilience/scenario3_slow_boot_test.go) proves a real boot's cumulative elapsed time CAN legitimately exceed FirstConnectBudget while never being suspected, as long as boot-progress pings keep arriving under SteadyHeartbeatBudget apart. No single platform.Timeouts constant is therefore a literal ceiling on this metric; 240s is kept as a CHOSEN (not derived) threshold — platform/timeouts.go's own 'not specified; chosen' convention — reused because it is the only concrete figure this codebase assigns to 'how long boot is expected to comfortably take as a whole' (§3.2's own FirstConnectBudget framing), not because the watchdog enforces it here. See docs/SLOS.md's own SLO 1 for the full corrected reasoning.

alerts.name: SpawnLatencyP95High
alerts.description: Real provider spawn/restore/resume calls are taking as long as the worst-case cold start this system's whole timeout hierarchy was calibrated against.
alerts.thresholdDerivation: 220s is platform.Timeouts.ProviderWorstColdStart (internal/platform/timeouts.go, §4.1's own '220s+' floor) — the figure ProviderHTTPClientTimeout (5m) is required to clear with margin (§5.4's own invariant chain: 'providerHTTPClientTimeout > provider worst cold start'). A p95 spawn latency at or above it means the provider's real-world performance has drifted past what the rest of the hierarchy assumes.

alerts.name: WatchdogFalseAlarmRateHigh
alerts.description: A meaningful fraction of watchdog activations are turning out to be wrong — the sandbox was alive the whole time.
alerts.condition: ratio(watchdog_false_alarm_total, watchdog_activation_total) > 0.10 over 30m, minimum 5 activations in the window
alerts.thresholdDerivation: §5.3 states a target of '~0' but gives no numeric figure, and no platform.Timeouts constant governs a RATE (a behavioral property, not a fixed duration) — this threshold is an explicit judgment call, not derived from a Go constant, following platform/timeouts.go's own 'not specified; chosen' convention for exactly this situation, flagged as a choice rather than presented as derived. 10% sits well above the occasional single-heartbeat-racing-the-boundary noise the two-budget liveness model (internal/domain/sandbox/liveness.go) can produce on its own. The minimum-activation floor avoids a misleading ratio from a tiny sample (e.g. 1-of-1 reading as 100%).

alerts.name: AutoMergeAuthDeadLetterAny
alerts.description: internal/app/automerge.Worker's own authGuard dead-lettered a scope (the shared worker-wide bot credential, or one repository) after exhausting domain/automerge.MaxAuthFailures consecutive authentication/permission-classified GitHub failures — auto-merge has stopped for the affected scope until an operator rotates the credential/redeploys (worker-wide) or investigates the repository's own access (per-repository), docs/TECHNICAL_PLAN.md §17.
alerts.thresholdDerivation: Presence, not a rate, mirroring OutboxDeadLetterAny's own identical reasoning immediately below: dead-lettering only happens once per scope, ever, after domain/automerge.MaxAuthFailures (5) consecutive classified failures are exhausted (internal/app/automerge/authguard.go) — there is no 'normal' rate of a credential or a repository's own access permanently failing, so any occurrence at all is worth a look. No runbook yet (this alert's own introduction, alongside the metric instrument it references) -- Runbook is left empty rather than pointed at an unrelated existing page.

alerts.name: TurnFalseFailureAny
alerts.description: A turn the control plane terminalized Failed on its own turn_deadline inference was, in fact, still genuinely working and finished successfully.
alerts.thresholdDerivation: Any occurrence: unlike an orphan reap, a turn_false_failure_total increment has no documented benign single-race explanation — every one means platform.Timeouts.TurnDeadline (60m, internal/platform/timeouts.go — 'chosen with margin below SupervisorTurnCap') fired on a turn that was, in fact, still genuinely working. Worth a look every time, not just above some rate.
